overlooked_assumption: The code assumes `end` is always a valid calendar date that remains valid when subtracting 5 years, ignoring that February 29 of a leap year shifts to a non-leap year where February has only 28 days.
why_it_breaks: When `end` is February 29 of a leap year (e.g., 2024), calling `end.replace(year=end.year - 5)` attempts to create February 29 of the target year. If the target year is not a leap year (e.g., 2019), the `day=29` is out of range for February, raising `ValueError: day is out of range for month`. The agent assumed year arithmetic on dates would always succeed, but did not account for calendar validity when crossing leap-year boundaries.
